answer: Temporal trust-edge aging resists sybils: a vouch edge only reaches full trust weight after it has PERSISTED across many epochs, so freshly-minted mutual-vouching among new fakes carries almost nothing. An echo of fakes all vouching for each other at creation forms edges that are age-zero and weightless; the copper patina of genuine long-standing honest edges carries the trust. A cipher-ring spun up overnight cannot fast-forward edge age — it must maintain the fake graph intact across many real epochs before its internal vouches count, exposing it to detection throughout.
